pale_blue_triangular_wash.description: A large flat watercolor wash of pale teal-blue applied behind the plant illustration, forming a roughly triangular or arrowhead shape with its apex at the top-center of the page and its base spanning the mid-page. This wash is entirely decorative and background-layer — it sits beneath the stem, leaves, flowers, and text lines. COLOR: semi-transparent teal-blue wash, approximately #8bbcb0 at its densest center, fading to near-invisible at the edges. The triangle's apex is at approximately (x=480, y=60) and its base extends from approximately (x=200, y=450) to (x=700, y=450). The wash interacts with text in the upper paragraph block (lines 1–11): the text is written OVER the wash on the parchment surface, and the wash is slightly visible beneath the ink. The triangular wash does not cause any text bisection — it is a purely tonal background element.

central_main_stem.description: The primary vertical axis of the plant. A slender, tall stem rendered in medium green ink outline with a lighter green fill wash inside. Runs from the root crown at approximately y=870 straight up to the apex flower cluster at approximately y=125. The stem is notably thin — approximately 20–25 normalized units wide in the text zone — creating a relatively narrow bisection gap compared to, e.g., f1v's broader stem. It passes directly through the center of the page, dividing both the upper paragraph block (lines 1–11) and the lower two-column block (lines 12–17) into left and right segments.

apex_flower_cluster.description: The topmost and most prominent flower structure at the crown of the plant. Consists of 3 open tubular/bell-shaped flowers arranged in a tight cluster on short pedicels. Each flower has: (1) reflexed/spreading petals in vivid red-orange, (2) prominent stamens or pistils extending outward in blue-violet, (3) a green calyx at the base. The tricolor scheme — red, blue, green — is the visual signature of all flowers on this folio. The apex cluster is the most fully open of the three flower groups and the most pigmented. Situated directly above the text zone at the top of the central stem.

color.petals: vivid red-orange, ~#d94f2b — the most saturated red on the page
color.stamens_pistils: medium blue-violet, ~#3a4fa0 — 3–4 thin lines per flower extending beyond petals
color.pedicels: thin green lines, same green as stem

left_upper_flower.description: A second flower group on a lateral branch extending from the upper-left side of the main stem, at approximately y=240–310. This appears to be a single flower or tight pair, slightly less fully open than the apex cluster. The branch angles upper-left from the stem. The tricolor (red/blue/green) is identical to the apex cluster.

color.petals: red-orange, ~#d94f2b, same hue as apex flowers

right_lower_flower.description: A third flower on a lateral branch extending from the right side of the stem at approximately y=450–530. Positioned lower on the stem than the left_upper_flower. The branch angles upper-right. The flower appears slightly smaller and is painted with slightly less pigment saturation, possibly because the scribe/illustrator painted this last and had less red pigment loaded. Still clearly tricolor.

color.petals: red-orange, ~#d94f2b, possibly slightly less saturated than apex

upper_left_leaf_pair.description: The highest pair of opposite leaves on the main stem, immediately below the apex flower cluster. Broad ovoid leaves with a pointed tip and slightly serrated or smooth edge. The left leaf extends upper-left, the right extends upper-right from the stem. Both are solidly filled with teal green.

color.midrib: implied by slight tonal variation, no separate color

mid_left_large_leaf.description: A large, broad, ovoid leaf on the left side of the mid-stem, the largest single leaf on the left side of the plant. It extends significantly to the left, reaching well into the left text column zone and constraining the left-side text width in the upper paragraph. Its base attaches to the stem at approximately y=430.

color.size_note: the largest leaf on the folio — its left tip reaches to approximately x=140

mid_right_large_leaf.description: The counterpart large leaf on the right side of the mid-stem, extending significantly to the right. Comparable in size to mid_left_large_leaf. Its base attaches at approximately y=400.

lower_left_leaf_pair.description: The lowest pair of large leaves on the left side of the stem, at approximately y=570–700. Two overlapping broad leaves extend left and lower-left. These are in the transition zone between the upper paragraph block and the lower two-column block.

color.fill: teal green, ~#3a7a5a, slightly lighter than upper leaves — possibly less pigment applied

lower_right_leaf_pair.description: The lowest leaves on the right side of the stem, extending right and lower-right at approximately y=600–730. Two broad ovoid leaves. Below these, the stem continues bare to the root.

root_system.description: The exposed root structure at the base of the central stem, drawn in a warm ochre-brown pigment that is sharply distinct from the green of the stem. Shows 3–4 radiating root arms spreading horizontally and slightly downward from the stem base, suggesting a fibrous or tuberous root. The roots occupy the lower margin of the parchment below the two-column text block. The color change from green (stem) to brown (root) is one of the most visually striking features of this folio — it appears to be intentional botanical illustration of the below-ground anatomy.

color.primary: warm ochre-brown, ~#b8752a — distinct from any other color used on the folio
color.outline: same ochre-brown ink, slightly darker for the outline strokes
color.note: NO green anywhere in the root zone — deliberate color separation between above-ground (green) and below-ground (brown) anatomy

right_margin_binding_strip.description: The right physical edge of the parchment where the folio is sewn into the binding. A narrow strip of natural parchment with binding thread or edge reinforcement visible. No illustration or text in this zone.

isolated_zones.status: Text written directly over the wash — wash is background, not a text-exclusion zone
isolated_zones.description: The large pale teal-blue watercolor triangle (x:200–700, y:60–455) does NOT exclude text — all 11 upper-block lines are written over it. The wash is a tonal/decorative background painted before the text was written (or concurrently), not a later addition. Its triangular shape mirrors the pointed silhouette of the plant as a whole. The blue color (~#8bbcb0) is unique on this folio — only used for this wash; all other colors are green (plant), red-orange (petals), blue-violet (stamens), brown (roots), cream (parchment), and brown (ink).

The tricolor red/blue/green flowers are the topmost illustration element. No text contacts or contours around this flower cluster.

isolated_zones.status: Active bisection agent — causes DOUBLE <-> in lines 3 and 4
isolated_zones.description: The left_upper_flower (x:245–330, y:220–325) is a critical bisection element. Its lateral branch/pedicel crosses through the left text column at y:195–256 (lines 3 and 4), creating the secondary gap in the double-bisection of those two lines. The flower itself is painted in the red-orange/blue-violet/green tricolor scheme. After y:256 the branch has passed above the text line positions and the double-bisection resolves back to a single-bisection from line 5 onward.

The right_lower_flower (x:560–650, y:430–540) sits in the gap between the upper paragraph block (which ends at y~473 with 'sorain') and the lower two-column block (which begins at y~822). This entire mid-page zone (y:473–822) is text-free illustration space dominated by the large leaves, bare mid-stem, and the right_lower_flower on its branch.

The mid_left_large_leaf (x:140–455, y:390–560) does not cause a <-> bisection (it touches the left margin, not the text center) but it significantly narrows the left-column text width in lines 9–11 by pushing x_min rightward from ~130 to ~200–240. This constraint is directly visible in the progressively shorter left segments of lines 9 ('shol.orchl'), 10 ('scharchy'), and 11 ('sorain'). The leaf's green color (~#3a7a5a) makes it visually dominant in this zone.

isolated_zones.status: Completely text-free — below lower text block
isolated_zones.description: The root system (x:310–620, y:870–970) sits between the lower text block's bottom-left column (which ends at approximately y=976 with f8v.16 left segment) and the absolute page bottom. The warm ochre-brown color (~#b8752a) is entirely distinct from every other element on the page — it is the only non-green, non-red, non-blue color used in the plant illustration. The three or four radiating root arms spread laterally from the stem base in a schematic depiction of a fibrous root system. No text interacts with the root illustration.

isolated_zones.status: Completely text-free / Large leaf and stem zone
isolated_zones.description: The entire zone between the two text blocks — approximately y:473–822 — is text-free. This is a very large negative-text space (~350 normalized units tall, roughly one third of the full page height) entirely occupied by the plant illustration: large teal-green leaves (mid and lower pairs), bare central stem, and the right_lower_flower. The absence of text in this zone is unusual compared to some herbal folios where text wraps around leaves more tightly; here the scribe gave the illustration full vertical dominance over the central third of the page.
